terra.problem: The passage says Jonathan had a thousand men with him at Gibeah. It does not say he took them there or that he was young.
The text says the Philistines heard about the attack, not that they found out on their own.
“Not at Gilgal yet” implies the Philistines will go there, which the passage does not say.
The passage says the troops began to desert Saul, not that the crowd grew thinner every day.
The explanation says the troops deserted because Samuel did not come. The passage does not give that as their reason.
“Who ends up offering them” implies both kinds of offering are offered. The text says Saul offered the burnt offering.
“No joke from me here” comments on how Papa Dorin is telling the passage.
The explanation is flat and repeats that Samuel did not say wisely without adding a useful distinction.
The explanation repeats the answer and says the word makes a difference without explaining the distinction between a command and a promise.
“A ruler, not a prophet” rules out the man being a prophet. Samuel does not say that.
“Nobody goes home” makes a claim about everyone that the passage does not make. It says the Philistines camped at Michmash.
The text gives the raiders' directions, but does not say how much ground they covered or that they covered it at one time.
“Keep your neighbors unarmed” overstates the text. The Philistines sought to prevent the Hebrews from making swords or spears, and Saul and Jonathan had weapons.
Calling it the Philistines' rule adds a formal rule the passage does not state. It reports what the Philistines had said.
“In the whole army” broadens the text's statement about the troops with Saul and Jonathan.
“The six hundred came with empty hands” goes beyond the text, which says the troops had no sword or spear.
